title: Looping with Lists
description: Use for loops to process list items and build new lists.

subtasks.title: List Recap - 1
subtasks.explainer:
# Lists

A list stores several items in one variable.

```python
pets = ["cat", "dog", "rabbit"]
```

Use `python:.append()` to add an item, `python:.remove()` to remove a named value, and `python:.pop()` to remove an item by index or remove the final item.
subtasks.leftContent:
# Last Lesson

1. What is a list?
2. Which method adds an item?
3. Which method removes the final item?
4. What number does indexing start at?

subtasks.title: List Recap - 2
subtasks.explainer: Match each list tool to its job.

pairs.answer: Adds an item to the end
Removes an item by index, or the final item

subtasks.title: Looping Through a List - 1
subtasks.explainer:
# Visit Every Item

A `python:for` loop can visit every item in a list.

```python
fruits = ["apple", "banana"]

for fruit in fruits:
  print(fruit)
```

On the first iteration, `python:fruit` stores `python:"apple"`. On the second iteration, it stores `python:"banana"`.

subtasks.title: Looping Through a List - 2
subtasks.explainer:
What does this code print?

```python
fruits = ["apple", "banana"]
for fruit in fruits:
  print(fruit)
```

options.feedback: This loop visits the list items directly, not their indexes.
The loop variable stores one current item at a time.

subtasks.title: Looping Through a List - 4
subtasks.explainer:
Why is this loop header wrong?

```python
for fruit in fruit:
  print(fruit)
```

options.text: It tries to loop through `python:fruit` instead of the list called `python:fruits`.

options.feedback: A `python:for` loop can iterate directly through a list.

options.text: The loop variable must be called `python:i`.
options.feedback: The loop variable can have a meaningful name such as `python:fruit`.

subtasks.title: Messages from List Items - 1
subtasks.explainer:
# F-Strings Inside Loops

An f-string can include the current list item.

```python
fruits = ["apple", "banana"]

for fruit in fruits:
  print(f"I love to eat {fruit}!")
```

The same print statement creates a different message on each iteration.

subtasks.title: Build a Shopping List - 1
subtasks.explainer:
# Build a New List

A loop can update another list during each iteration.

```python
for item in friend_items:
  shopping_list.append(item)
```

The loop variable `python:item` stores one current value at a time.

subtasks.title: Build a Shopping List - 2
subtasks.explainer:
Why is this line wrong inside the loop?

```python
shopping_list.append(friend_items)
```

options.text: It appends the whole list instead of the current `python:item`.
`python:.append()` cannot be used inside a loop.
options.feedback: Methods can be called inside a loop.
Variable names can vary. The important part is appending the current item.

subtasks.starterCode:

shopping_list = []

for item in friend_items:
  # Append the current item.
  # Print a message using an f-string.

print(shopping_list)
subtasks.completeCode:
friend_items = ["cookies", "juice", "bananas"]
shopping_list = []

for item in friend_items:
  shopping_list.append(item)

check.hint: Append `python:item`, print one f-string message inside the loop, then print the finished list after the loop.
Append the current `python:item`, not the whole `python:friend_items` list.

subtasks.explainer: Match each list-loop idea to its meaning.

pairs.answer: Adds the current item to a list

subtasks.title: Final Recap - 2
subtasks.explainer:
What does this code print?

```python
pets = ["cat", "dog", "rabbit"]
for pet in pets:
  print(f"Hello {pet}")
```

options.feedback: The f-string inserts the current value stored in `python:pet`.
The output also includes the word `python:Hello`.
The loop prints one message for each list item.

subtasks.title: Final Recap - 3
subtasks.explainer:
- A `python:for` loop can visit every item in a list.
- The loop variable stores the current item.
- An f-string can include the current item in a message.
- `python:.append(item)` can build a second list one item at a time.

Next lesson, we will ask whether a loop can visit each character in a string.
